summary: Updates several BGP Extended Community registries, replacing the Experimental Use registration procedure in some entries because their use is clearly not experimental and the label is misleading. It updates RFC 7153 and RFC 8955.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC corrects registration procedures and names in several BGP Extended Community registries. It removes an Experimental Use label where the RFC says that label does not match the primary use.

questions: what is first come first served registration
what did rfc 9184 change in bgp registries
subtitle: Correcting registration procedures and names in BGP Extended Community registries.

tldr.problem: Some BGP Extended Community types were marked for Experimental Use even though their primary use and related subtypes were not experimental.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes types 0x80–0x82 to First Come First Served and removes “Experimental Use” from three related subtype registry names.
tldr.outcome: The update changes several registries and updates RFCs 7153 and 8955.

today: RFC 9184 is a Standards Track document that updates RFC 7153 and RFC 8955. It revises the BGP Extended Community registry procedures and subtype registry names.

sections.title: Why the Registry Labels Changed
sections.content:
RFC 7153 organized the IANA registries for BGP Extended Community type and subtype values. The BGP Transitive Extended Community Types registry included values 0x80–0x8F for Experimental Use, but the primary use of types 0x80, 0x81, and 0x82 and their subtype registries was non-experimental.

RFC 9184 updates RFCs 7153 and 8955 to make the registry procedures and names reflect that use.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry called some values experimental even though their primary use was not experimental. This RFC changes those entries and related registry names.

sections.title: Type and Subtype Registry Updates
sections.content:
For type values 0x80–0x82, IANA changed the registration procedure to First Come First Served. Values 0x83–0x8F remain Reserved for Experimental Use, and the other ranges retain their listed procedures.

The RFC also removes “Experimental Use” from the names of the three Generic Transitive Extended Community subtype registries. It adds RFC 9184 as a reference for the affected registry entries.
sections.plainLanguage: Types 0x80–0x82 now use First Come First Served. The experimental designation remains for 0x83–0x8F, and the subtype registry names no longer say “Experimental Use.”

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that there are no direct security considerations arising from this document. Its changes concern registry procedures and names.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC identifies no direct security considerations for these registry changes.
